discovery.title: What happens here?
discovery.body: The AI asks simple questions, one at a time, to draft your app's plan: what it does, which screens it has and what it stores. Nothing is built before you approve the plan.

architecture.title: Why plan before building?
architecture.body: The specialist organizes the app, checks current official sources and turns each requirement into a test guarantee. This reduces rework without exposing technical complexity.

database.title: What is a database?
database.body: It's like an organized notebook where your app writes everything down — each kind of information (customers, orders…) becomes a card with columns. You see it all in the Your data tab.

design.title: Why screens first?
design.body: We build the look with example data first, so you can see and adjust without waiting. Click any part of the app to request changes.

backend.title: What does "make it work" mean?
backend.body: The invisible part: actually saving what you type, fetching the right information and protecting what needs a password.

review.title: What gets checked?
review.body: The AI tests the whole app, hunts for errors and verifies security items (protected passwords, data stored the right way) before allowing publication.

launch.title: What is Cloudflare?
launch.body: It's the service (free to start) where your app will live on the internet. Connect your account with one click and the app gets its own shareable address.

stageMessage.discovery: Let's start! I want to create an app and need your help planning it. Ask me ONE question at a time using the ask_user tool, in plain language with no technical terms, to understand: what the app does, who uses it, which screens it needs, what information it stores, whether people log in, which important rules exist, how I will know it is ready, and what stays out of the first version. Whenever the question has choices, pass options (2 to 8) with allow_freeform: true — so I can click a button OR type my own answer. When the question allows picking SEVERAL options (e.g. which screens, what data to store, login methods), pass multi_select: true. When you have everything, save the plan with app_save_spec including requirements, run app_spec_audit, show me a simple summary and ask if I approve. Always speak my language.
stageMessage.architecture: Plan how this app will be built. Read the spec and its history. If an architecture decision requires changing product behavior, scope, data, access, or acceptance criteria, confirm it with me and propose a versioned spec revision before continuing. Otherwise, research only current official documentation for the recommended stack, record the sources, and create a versioned architecture with a traceable test plan. Every acceptance criterion, rule, behavior, entity and login requirement must have at least one test. Save with app_save_architecture, run app_architecture_audit, and submit the architecture stage with app_submit_stage. Explain the result in plain language.
stageMessage.database: Let's store the app's data: create the migrations from the approved plan (app_get_spec), write realistic examples in seeds/seed.sql, apply with app_provision_db and double-check. When done, deliver the stage with app_submit_stage and explain in one simple sentence what was done.
stageMessage.design: Let's build the plan's screens: build each screen with example data (lib/mock) so I can watch the app take shape, record each screen with app_record_feature AFTER checking it in the preview, and tell me to look. When they're all ready, deliver with app_submit_stage.
stageMessage.backend: Now make the app really work: create the API routes for every piece of information in the plan, switch the screens from example data to real data, and if the plan has login, set up authentication securely. Verify everything in the preview, record with app_record_feature and deliver with app_submit_stage.
stageMessage.review: Run the quality check: test the whole app in the preview as if you were me, fix any errors, and write the REVIEW.md report in words I understand. When everything is green, deliver with app_submit_stage.
